After someone has left the house the robot is asked about chore things (vacuum cleaner, laundry basket, dog bowl, watering can). So what matters is where each object is WHILE IN USE and just before, at the time of day that use happens, not only where it rests between uses.

About 10 minutes after each question the resident tells the robot where the object turned out to be; those show up in the sightings below like any other sighting.

Confidence is the probability, from 0 to 1, that the spot you name is right. Low numbers are expected when the evidence is thin: about 0.3 means a guess among several plausible spots, about 0.6 means it is the most likely spot but it could easily be elsewhere, about 0.9 means you have seen it there repeatedly at this time of day and nothing has changed. Do not give the same number every time.

After someone has left the house the robot is asked about chore things (vacuum cleaner, laundry basket, dog bowl, watering can). So what matters is where each object is WHILE IN USE and just before, at the time of day that use happens, not only where it rests between uses.

About 10 minutes after each question the resident tells the robot where the object turned out to be; those show up in the sightings below like any other sighting.

Answer with one spot name from the list above (the object is somewhere in the house; if it is being used or carried right now, name the spot it is most likely to be at or next to).

Confidence is the probability, from 0 to 1, that the spot you name is right. Low numbers are expected when the evidence is thin: about 0.3 means a guess among several plausible spots, about 0.6 means it is the most likely spot but it could easily be elsewhere, about 0.9 means you have seen it there repeatedly at this time of day and nothing has changed. Do not give the same number every time.

Reply with JSON: {"reasoning": one or two short sentences on what the sightings, the time of day and the residents' routine suggest, "location": one spot name, "confidence": number from 0 to 1}

After someone has left the house the robot is asked about chore things (vacuum cleaner, laundry basket, dog bowl, watering can). So what matters is where each object is WHILE IN USE and just before, at the time of day that use happens, not only where it rests between uses.

About 10 minutes after each question the resident tells the robot where the object turned out to be; those show up in the sightings below like any other sighting.

Answer with one spot name from the list above (the object is somewhere in the house; if it is being used or carried right now, name the spot it is most likely to be at or next to).

Confidence is the probability, from 0 to 1, that the spot you name is right. Low numbers are expected when the evidence is thin: about 0.3 means a guess among several plausible spots, about 0.6 means it is the most likely spot but it could easily be elsewhere, about 0.9 means you have seen it there repeatedly at this time of day and nothing has changed. Do not give the same number every time.

After someone has left the house the robot is asked about chore things (vacuum cleaner, laundry basket, dog bowl, watering can). So what matters is where each object is WHILE IN USE and just before, at the time of day that use happens, not only where it rests between uses.

About 10 minutes after each question the resident tells the robot where the object turned out to be; those show up in the sightings below like any other sighting.

Answer with one spot name from the list above (the object is somewhere in the house; if it is being used or carried right now, name the spot it is most likely to be at or next to).

Confidence is the probability, from 0 to 1, that the spot you name is right. Low numbers are expected when the evidence is thin: about 0.3 means a guess among several plausible spots, about 0.6 means it is the most likely spot but it could easily be elsewhere, about 0.9 means you have seen it there repeatedly at this time of day and nothing has changed. Do not give the same number every time.

After someone has left the house the robot is asked about chore things (vacuum cleaner, laundry basket, dog bowl, watering can). So what matters is where each object is WHILE IN USE and just before, at the time of day that use happens, not only where it rests between uses.

About 10 minutes after each question the resident tells the robot where the object turned out to be; those show up in the sightings below like any other sighting.

Answer with one spot name from the list above (the object is somewhere in the house; if it is being used or carried right now, name the spot it is most likely to be at or next to).

Confidence is the probability, from 0 to 1, that the spot you name is right. Low numbers are expected when the evidence is thin: about 0.3 means a guess among several plausible spots, about 0.6 means it is the most likely spot but it could easily be elsewhere, about 0.9 means you have seen it there repeatedly at this time of day and nothing has changed. Do not give the same number every time.

Reply with JSON: {"reasoning": one or two short sentences on what the sightings, the time of day and the residents' routine suggest, "location": one spot name, "confidence": number from 0 to 1}

So what matters is where each object is WHILE IN USE and just before, at the time of day that use happens, not only where it rests between uses.

Low numbers are expected when the evidence is thin: about 0.3 means a guess among several plausible spots, about 0.6 means it is the most likely spot but it could easily be elsewhere, about 0.9 means you have seen it there repeatedly at this time of day and nothing has changed. Do not give the same number every time.

After someone has left the house the robot is asked about chore things (vacuum cleaner, laundry basket, dog bowl, watering can). So what matters is where each object is WHILE IN USE and just before, at the time of day that use happens, not only where it rests between uses.

About 10 minutes after each question the resident tells the robot where the object turned out to be; those show up in the sightings below like any other sighting.

Answer with one spot name from the list above (the object is somewhere in the house; if it is being used or carried right now, name the spot it is most likely to be at or next to).

Confidence is the probability, from 0 to 1, that the spot you name is right. Low numbers are expected when the evidence is thin: about 0.3 means a guess among several plausible spots, about 0.6 means it is the most likely spot but it could easily be elsewhere, about 0.9 means you have seen it there repeatedly at this time of day and nothing has changed. Do not give the same number every time.
